I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is what fits my fields, the water conditions, and the weather best. At the start of the growing season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage that through spring and harvest it in early summer, then I will plant summer maize right after. I will do this because it is the most familiar system for me, the easiest to sell, and the safest way for me to get grain from the land every year. I do not want to take big risks on crops that need more skill, more labor, or have unstable prices.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, give moderate fertilizer, water it a few times if water is available, and spray only when disease or insects are clearly a problem. After harvest, I will quickly prepare the land and plant hybrid summer maize, because maize gives steady yield here and matches the season well. I will put more nitrogen on maize than wheat, use some phosphorus and potassium on both, and keep field work simple with rotary tillage so I can finish on time without too much labor. I am choosing a steady, practical plan that protects yield and keeps my workload manageable.
